subject: Equinox Health — private hosting constraints and deal desk approval request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lang <sara@equinoxhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Equinox pilot follow-up — hosting constraints

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — glad the latency profile looked good for your diagnostics use case. I promised to follow up with a concise summary of what we can do for a private deployment and where I'm asking for an exception.

Short summary for your procurement/legal team:
- Model serving in a private VPC (customer-owned) hosted in your on-prem colo.
- No outbound egress from the cluster (no telemetry, no remote KV replication).
- KMS/HSM integration for key control, customer-managed keys.
- Extended audit access window (90 days of requestable raw logs for incident investigation).
- Redwood to provide on-site engineering support for initial rollout (2 weeks) — after that we would need a support access model.

Per what we discussed, there are three items that need approver signoff on our side: a) no-egress requirement (means we must ship a fully air-gapped package), b) extended 90-day raw log access (longer than our standard 30-day incident window), and c) a one-time pilot credit / discount to offset engineering setup.

I'm looping in Marissa (deal desk) and Kim (legal) to outline the redlines and get an internal path to approval. Attaching the draft SOW and the customer's redline doc for reference.

Next step: Sara — can you confirm the provisioning timeline and whether Equinox will accept a one-time on-prem installation fee + monthly hosting? After I have that, I'll ask for the executive variance.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192
From: Sara Lang <sara@equinoxhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Equinox pilot follow-up — hosting constraints

Jonas,

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side (procurement + security):
1) No egress — correct, we need the inference cluster to have zero outbound connections except to our internal monitoring stack. No external telemetry by policy.
2) Audit window — 90 days is acceptable for now, but we will likely ask to extend to 180 days after the pilot depending on compliance findings. Please surface any technical blockers.
3) On-site support — we require Redwood engineers to be able to access the environment for initial deployment. We can agree to a signed SOW and a short-term VPN/access model; continuing access will require written approval from our security team.
4) Pricing — procurement is looking for a pilot credit to cover 60% of the initial engineering effort plus a temporary 25% discount on monthly reserved capacity for the first 3 months.

Attached is our procurement redline (Legal_Redlines_Equinox.docx). We're targeting a Dec 6th start date for the pilot. Can you route for internal approval this week?

Best,
Sara Lang
Director, Procurement | Equinox Health
procurement@equinoxhealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Equinox pilot follow-up — exec approval request (no-egress, extended audit, pilot credit)

Team — forwarding Equinox's constraints and ask. Key ask from customer:
- No egress (air-gapped/no external telemetry) — requires an ops delivery bundle and signoff from infra on support model.
- Extended audit access: 90 days now, potential request for 180 later.
- Pricing: pilot credit covering ~60% of engineering setup + 25% monthly discount for months 1-3.

Attached: EQX_SOW_draft.pdf, Legal_Redlines_20261101.docx (their redlines summarized inline).

Recommendation (ops/technical): Priyom — can the infra team deliver an air-gapped package for a one-time engineering install? What are the residual operational risks (support/access, security posture) and any additional one-time fees?

Recommendation (commercial/legal): Marissa / Kim — given the strategic signal (large regional hospital chain, potential multi-region expansion) I'm proposing we consider a capped pilot concession: a one-time credit up to $45k (covers ~60% of effort) + a transient 20% discount (months 1-3). If we accept extended 90 day audit window as-is we need to limit scope to metadata + redacted logs; full raw logs would require SOC justification and an SLA carveout.

Requesting Hannah's executive variance to approve the pilot concession and allow our legal team to negotiate a narrow raw-log access clause restricted to incident investigations with customer-signed NDA and audit trail.

Thanks — Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Equinox pilot follow-up — exec approval request (no-egress, extended audit, pilot credit)

Hannah — quick summary and ask:
- Account: Equinox Health (regional hospital chain) — pilot Start target: 2026-12-06.
- Commercial ask: One-time pilot credit ~$45k (to be taken as upfront credit against first invoice) + temporary 20% discount on reserved capacity months 1-3.
- Contractual ask: No-egress clause (air-gapped) + 90-day raw log access for incident review (customer may push to 180 later).
- Legal redlines attached; they want raw logs and unlimited access for internal auditors. Kim proposes: allow redacted/raw access only under narrow incident definitions, with customer-triggered request and our logging access performed by Redwood-administered export and audit trail.

Risk/ops notes from Priyom: delivering air-gapped on-prem installer is doable but requires a $12k one-time engineering setup fee (3 engineer-weeks) and documented support boundaries. Long-term support access without direct remote outbound channels will force on-call travel or pre-approved bastion access under strict temporary access windows (adds ops overhead).

My recommendation: Approve the pilot credit capped at $45k total, require a $12k one-time install fee to be invoiced (reduces net concession), and set the discount at 20% months 1-3. Legal to accept 90 days limited raw-log access for incident investigations only, with strict NDA and one-way export process that Redwood controls. If Hannah approves, Marissa/legal will finalize the wording and I will prepare the revenue-impact memo for Deal Desk.

Request: Hannah — please confirm OK/no-go by COB 2026-11-03 so we can meet Equinox's procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Equinox pilot follow-up — exec approval request (no-egress, extended audit, pilot credit)

Team — after reviewing the trade-offs I approve the following, with conditions:
1) Commercial concession: Approve a capped pilot concession up to $45,000 gross. The deal must include a $12,000 one-time install fee (invoiced to customer) so net concession is $33,000. No further discounting beyond the 20% for months 1-3 without explicit VP sales escalation.
2) No-egress / air-gap: Approved for the pilot only. Engineering (Priyom) to provide a documented runbook and support boundaries. Any request to extend air-gap beyond the pilot requires a separate exec approval.
3) Audit/raw logs: Approve 90-day requestable raw log access limited to incident investigations. Legal (Kim) to add precise language: customer requests must meet incident criteria, Redwood performs the export, redaction process in place, access requires customer NDA amendment and an audit trail. If customer later requests 180 days, bring back to me.
4) SOW & timeline: Jonas to communicate approval to Equinox along with a firm SOW and the one-time install fee and timeline (Dec 6 start acceptable if engineering can commit).

Marissa — please draft the approval clause, updated revenue-impact memo, and attach the signed SOW before any work begins. Kim — please prepare the log-access clause and temporary access language for the SOW. Priyom — confirm resource availability for a Dec 6 start and the travel/access plan.

I'll sign off on the final SOW and term sheet once legal and deal desk upload the updated artifacts.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
